description:
SELF-OPTIMISATION, lab side (2026-07-10) -- the AGENT'S OWN EFFICIENCY OBJECTIVE for the self-experiment machinery. seeds/comprehension_health.json is the SENSE (the agent notices its comprehension process is slow/divergent and files a SelfConcern{kind:'performance'|'comprehension'}); this seed is what lets a PROMOTED concern of that kind run an experiment that is actually judged on SPEED, not just correctness.

The wiring (all mechanical host I/O except the two rules below, per CLAUDE.md): scripts/jabberwock_daemon.py's _promote_relations_for_concern routes a performance/comprehension-kind concern into the SAME conversation experiment bundle (test/replay/send/judge/adopt) a reply_fix concern gets, so the EXISTING composer machinery (reflective_faculty._compose_experiment_rule's conversation branch, seeds/variation_ops.json's reply_ablation family) authors a targeted reply-rule-ablation SeedDelta and dispatches it to scripts/convo_child_run.py exactly as before -- nothing about authoring or dispatch changes. Two mechanical additions make the CHILD's report carry a speed signal: convo_child_run.py now times each replayed probe and reports avg_turn_ms; domains/experiment_dispatch.py's _ingest_result carries it onto the Run and Experiment (the same 'copy what the child already decided' pattern as regressions); and _spawn mechanically copies the agent's OWN current shadow_latency_recent_avg onto the dispatched SeedDelta as baseline_avg_turn_ms + a performance_objective marker, ONLY when the Experiment's driving StandingConcern (found by axis_tag == StandingConcern.name, the same string key the mint rule already stamps) is kind 'performance' or 'comprehension' -- a mechanical copy, not a decision (which experiments get an efficiency objective is entirely the fact the AGENT already decided when it filed and a human promoted that concern's kind).

(1) judge_performance_experiment_outcome -- OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict (seeds carried by _compose_experiment_rule's 'judge' relation, unchanged and still installed -- it decides correctness/regression exactly as it always has) for ANY Experiment whose delta carries performance_objective==1.0: supported iff regressions==0 AND the child's avg_turn_ms improved on the recorded baseline; a regression always refutes regardless of speed; an unchanged or slower avg_turn_ms (no regressions) refutes; a tied avg_turn_ms is inconclusive (no-op delta). Sequenced to run AFTER the generic judge in the SAME run_rules fixpoint -- same two-stage pattern as seeds/adoption_safety.json's veto running after judge/before mark_adopt_ready, but with a DELIBERATE difference from that rule's shape, found live while gating this wave: the generic judge's own 'analysed' edge (added by ITS effects, not present at match time) must be a MATCH clause here (`[['exp','has_delta','delta'],['exp','analysed','run']]`), not merely something the `where` clause peeks at via a Neighbours/Exists Term. A where-only Exists(Neighbours(exp,'analysed')) evaluates correctly under a direct `native.evaluate()` probe but never re-fires the rule through run_rules() on the live daemon-shaped graph (500 seeds, hundreds of active rules) once 'has_delta' has stopped changing -- the engine's incremental re-match appears to be keyed off the rule's OWN match-clause edge types, not off edges a where-clause merely reads. Promoting 'analysed' into the match clause fixed it (confirmed both on a minimal repro and the live conversation-experiment pipeline). Documented here as an engine gotcha for the next rule that wants to sequence after another rule's edge-effect within one fixpoint: put the dependency edge in match, not where. The existing mark_adopt_ready_*/perform_adoptions/adopt_denied_on_regression machinery is UNCHANGED downstream: it reads exp.outcome + delta.act_rule_varied + exp.regressions exactly as before, so a performance experiment that judges 'supported' with a genuine reply-ablation delta and zero regressions is adopted through the SAME path a reply_fix experiment is, still vetoed by the regression guard if it ever disagrees with what this rule computed.

(2) note_experiments_exhausted -- THE HONEST TRAIL for 'the agent tried, and the self-experiment machinery could not find an adopting variant' (not scoped to performance -- any conversation-bundle concern whose every dispatched Experiment has reached a terminal state, none adopted, and none still requested/running gets this marker exactly once). This is where the known Rust-needing fix (the O(concepts x mentions) mention-resolution join cost named in docs/comprehension_decision_ledger.md) surfaces if/when the agent files it as its own performance gap and every ablation trial the composer can construct (seed-skip / reply-rule ablation) refutes or is inconclusive -- the agent FINDS that its available variation repertoire cannot fix a cost that lives in a join algorithm, not in a rule or a seed boundary, and says so honestly (surfaced by reflective_faculty._run_self_improvement_status) rather than looping forever or silently giving up. Rung-4 (world_adapter._self_extend_reflex / ExtensionProposal) stays the separate, still-human-gated path for actually building a new Rust primitive. || RESIDUAL-CLOSURE (v1.1.0): judge_knob_experiment_outcome -- the knob_edit (held-node-attr) variation family's verdict, judged on the family's direct observable from the child's CONTROLLED double-pass replay: variant_reforms vs control_reforms (fewer spurious reforms supports; tied is inconclusive; more refutes; regressions>0 always refutes). Per-pass shadow-latency means ride along as informational data. || WHERE-CLAUSE-VARIATION (v1.2.0): judge_rule_literal_outcome -- the rule_literal_edit variation family's verdict, judged on the family's own structural WITNESS fire-count from the child's CONTROLLED double-pass (control pass at the ORIGINAL rule, then the rule swap, then the variant pass -- see seeds/variation_ops.json's description). Correctness first, exactly like the knob judge: ANY regression refutes regardless of the witness delta. Then -- the difference from the knob judge, and the point of this rule -- the verdict is checked against WHAT THE CONCERN ASKED FOR, not a fixed sign: the delta's own `rule_literal_direction` ('increase_fires', from the concern's 'fires too rarely/never' wording, or 'decrease_fires', from 'fires too eagerly/often') selects which way the witness delta must move to support. `rule_literal_direction=='increase_fires'`: variant_witness_fires > control_witness_fires supports, equal is inconclusive, fewer refutes (the concern said the rule fires too rarely and the variant is meant to make it fire MORE). `rule_literal_direction=='decrease_fires'`: the mirror (fewer supports, equal is inconclusive, more refutes). This direction branch is a Term-level IfThenElse over the delta's own string attr, not a Python decision -- the SAME class of graph-native comparison the generic judge's score-sign IfThenElse already is; only the CHOICE of which comparison to run is data (the concern's own wording, read by `_compose_rule_literal_variant`'s direction lexicon at compose time). Same match-clause 'analysed' sequencing as the performance/knob judges (the engine-gotcha note above applies); OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict for rule_literal_edit deltas exactly as the other two family judges do for their own marker. || COMPOSER-CAPABILITY (v1.3.0): judge_datum_feedback_outcome / judge_shape_mint_outcome -- the two new families' verdicts, judged on their own direct observable (the interlocutor belief / decode_shape fit count, before vs after, from the child's controlled double-pass) exactly like the knob/rule-literal judges' own reforms/witness-fires comparisons -- correctness first (any regression refutes), then the family's own fixed comparison direction (datum-feedback: lower variant belief supports; shape-mint: higher variant fit supports).

rules.name: judge_knob_experiment_outcome
rules.comment: RESIDUAL-CLOSURE (knob_edit family, v1.1.0): the verdict for a held-threshold (knob) experiment, judged on the family's DIRECT observable -- 'fewer spurious reforms' -- from the child's own CONTROLLED double-pass report (scripts/convo_child_run.py: control pass at the parent's held value, then apply the knob delta, then the variant pass; same process, same warm caches -- the run-15 protected-control lesson, never a cold child vs a warm parent). Correctness first: ANY regression refutes regardless of the reform count (and seeds/adoption_safety.json's veto would deny adoption anyway); then strictly fewer reform marks in the variant pass supports, a tied count is inconclusive (the knob moved nothing observable), MORE reforms refutes -- a knob trial that measures worse REFUTES, never adopts (the residual-closure directive's honest-judge requirement). Same match-clause 'analysed' sequencing as the performance judge (the engine-gotcha note in this seed's description applies); OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict for knob deltas exactly as the performance judge does for performance_objective deltas. v1.3.0 (tranche 8): direction-aware -- delta.knob_direction=='increase_fires' supports MORE reform marks (the concern said the reform fires too rarely); absent/decrease_fires keeps the fewer-supports verdict.

rules.name: judge_rule_literal_outcome
rules.comment: WHERE-CLAUSE-VARIATION (rule_literal_edit family, v1.2.0): the verdict for a held-rule-literal experiment, judged on the family's DIRECT observable -- the picked rule's own structural WITNESS fire-count -- from the child's CONTROLLED double-pass report (scripts/convo_child_run.py: control pass at the ORIGINAL rule, then the rule swap, then the variant pass; same process, same warm caches -- the run-15 protected-control lesson, never a cold child vs a warm parent). Correctness first: ANY regression refutes regardless of the witness delta (and seeds/adoption_safety.json's veto would deny adoption anyway). Then the verdict is checked against WHAT THE CONCERN ASKED FOR (delta.rule_literal_direction, set by _compose_rule_literal_variant's direction lexicon at compose time): 'increase_fires' (the concern said the rule fires too rarely) supports iff variant_witness_fires > control_witness_fires; 'decrease_fires' (fires too eagerly) supports iff variant_witness_fires < control_witness_fires; either way an unchanged witness count is inconclusive (the literal shift moved nothing observable) and the wrong-way delta refutes. Same match-clause 'analysed' sequencing as the performance/knob judges (the engine-gotcha note in this seed's description applies); OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict for rule_literal_edit deltas exactly as the other two family judges do for their own marker.

rules.name: note_experiments_exhausted
effects: self-experiment machinery found no adopt-ready variant for this concern (every dispatched trial reached a terminal verdict and none qualified for adoption); may need a new primitive beyond composable seed/rule edits

rules.name: judge_datum_feedback_outcome
rules.comment: COMPOSER-CAPABILITY (datum_feedback_rule family, v1.3.0): the verdict for a datum-feedback experiment (a genuinely NEW, ADD-ONLY rule that feeds a recorded datum back into a held belief -- see reflective_faculty._compose_datum_feedback_rule), judged on the family's DIRECT observable -- the interlocutor belief's own before/after VALUE -- from the child's CONTROLLED double-pass report (scripts/convo_child_run.py: control pass with the authored rule absent, then install it, then the variant pass; same process, same warm caches -- the run-15 protected-control lesson, never a cold child vs a warm parent). Correctness first: ANY regression refutes regardless of the belief delta (and seeds/adoption_safety.json's veto would deny adoption anyway); then STRICTLY LOWER variant_belief than control_belief supports (the v1 fixed direction -- the belief moves DOWN as the datum accrues, matching the motivating case), a tied belief is inconclusive (the rule moved nothing observable -- e.g. the datum never changed during the replay), a HIGHER belief refutes. Same match-clause 'analysed' sequencing as the knob/rule-literal judges (the engine-gotcha note in this seed's description applies); OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict for datum_feedback_edit deltas exactly as the other family judges do for their own marker.

rules.name: judge_shape_mint_outcome
rules.comment: COMPOSER-CAPABILITY (shape_mint family, v1.3.0): the verdict for a shape-mint experiment (a brand-new InterlocutorShape constructed from a poor-fit party's own dominant accumulated features -- see reflective_faculty._compose_shape_mint), judged on the family's DIRECT observable -- decode_shape's own FIT COUNT for that party, before/after -- from the child's CONTROLLED double-pass report (scripts/convo_child_run.py: control pass with the minted shape absent, then install it via add_concepts, then the variant pass; same process, same warm caches -- the run-15 protected-control lesson). Correctness first: ANY regression refutes regardless of the fit delta (and seeds/adoption_safety.json's veto would deny adoption anyway); then STRICTLY HIGHER variant_belief (fit) than control_belief supports (the minted shape genuinely explains the party better), a tied fit is inconclusive (the mint moved nothing observable), a LOWER fit refutes. Same match-clause 'analysed' sequencing as the knob/rule-literal/datum-feedback judges (the engine-gotcha note in this seed's description applies); OVERRIDES the generic score-sign verdict for shape_mint_edit deltas exactly as the other family judges do for their own marker.

rules.name: close_abstained_variant
rules.comment: An empty (abstained) variant is closed without dispatch or credit -- measured tranche 10: 'sort' spent 3 real child replays on empty cue_set_edit deltas.
